longformArticle.deck: A careful account of the Cecil Hotel elevator footage, official finding, and the folklore mechanics of an empty elevator image.

storyBody.heading: Arrival and Quiet Routine
paragraphs: In late January 2013, a 21-year-old Canadian guest checked into a downtown Los Angeles hotel later identified in media accounts as the Cecil Hotel and prepared to continue a routine trip out to Santa Cruz. The sequence begins as ordinary civic infrastructure: check-in, rooms, elevator rides, and normal guest movement. That mundane beginning is the first hard boundary in the record.

storyBody.heading: Missing Call and Public Alarm
paragraphs: When daily contact with her family stopped, relatives reported her missing. Police treated the case as serious and moved quickly into public appeals and investigation. At that point, an ordinary absence stopped being a private household problem and became a public chain with documented institutional response.

storyBody.heading: The Elevator Footage and Last-Seen Moment
paragraphs: LAPD released still and moving camera records from a hotel elevator showing unusual late-night movements: repeated button presses, repeated exits, and a tense posture around the car doors and hallway edges. Authorities used the footage as a witness chain for the last known public appearances, while repeatedly stressing that the images were incomplete about motive and mental state.

storyBody.heading: Search and Roof-Route Check
paragraphs: Investigators and responders searched the building and surrounding structures, while officials and media later described rooftop access as controlled and alarmed in the official operational sense. The key effect was procedural: the unknown space narrowed into defined pathways, even while the exact movement path between last image and recovery remained unresolved.

storyBody.heading: Discovery in the Water System
paragraphs: On February 19, 2013, hotel maintenance staff found a body in a rooftop water tank during a low-pressure response visit from guests. Police identified the body as the missing guest and began the material sequence transition: from missing-person case to recovered-body case, with removal and examination now part of the chain.

storyBody.heading: Aftermath and Legend Formation
paragraphs: Coroner findings later ruled the manner of death as drowning and reported no drugs as a direct contributing factor in available statements, while acknowledging unresolved questions about exact access events. The case record is therefore finite in fact but open in interpretation. The surviving footage and tight elevator framing gave public culture a repeating template: an empty, controlled vertical space that feels like a liminal corridor.
